To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the imagined teacher, the perceived teacher and the actual teacher are not three different teachers, but three different aspects of one and the same teaching identity.
the imagined professional identities of pre-service teachers can be a powerful impetus to innovation and change.
the imagined professional self of future teachers, far from being a hindrance to their learning process, can be a powerful impetus towards innovation and change in the educational field.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the imagined identity that the future teachers have built, in interaction with the school reality, can be transformed into a professional identity that can be a powerful impetus to innovation and educational change.
how future teachers make meaning of their teaching experiences, and the implications that this may have for the development of their teaching identity.
the way that the imagined identity of future teachers, which they construct in their initial training and in their teaching practicum, influences their identity as teachers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the imagined teacher and the perceived teacher are two complementary elements of the teaching identity that student teachers build in the process of their professional socialization.

, the imagined identity of the teacher is the result of the interweaving between the imagined teacher and the perceived identity, and that this identity is the product of the interplay of the real and the ideal.
the ideal teacher, the imagined teacher and the teacher that is perceived by the student teacher are three distinct entities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the imagined professional teacher is the ideal teacher, and the ideal teacher is a real teacher.

we have found that the imagined professional teacher identity that the student teachers build is an important source of motivation, which can become a powerful force for change in the teaching profession.
we are trying to understand how the teaching identity of future teachers is built in their teaching practicum, and the implications of this for the future of education.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the imagined teacher is not a mere fantasy, but a real person who is able to influence the future of education.
the imagined professional teacher can be an important resource in the building of the teaching identity.
the imagined professional identities of future teachers can be a powerful resource to foster innovation and educational change in the classroom.
